I didn't actually think I would I like Metro 2033. Horror/Post-Apocalyptic is not usually my style. The game feels like it came out in the early 2000's, but in a charming sort of way. The animations and gameplay are simple, but that makes it even better. You aren't concerned all that much with the look (all great), but you can focus on the audio and atmosphere, and just appreciate the situation you are placed in.

Now that I have played both Metro 2033 Original and Redux I can say that I like the Redux version better. The Redux improved more than just textures, lighting and voice acting. It improved stealth as well as the layout of some areas. I had more fun in Redux because there is just more to do, However that doesn't mean I didn't enjoy the Original game as well.

If you're a fan of Stalker, you will most likely enjoy this game as it has very similar themes despite being chapter based rather than a non-linear, open world format. I remember when the Metro games were first released and now I have finally found time to play the campaigns. The story line is quite good, creatures are quite cool and the characters are mostly interesting esp towards the end. Apart from a few clunky aspects of gameplay, such as inability to pickup some items unless your proximity to them is just right, or difficulty climbing ladders and jumping to or from ledges, it was challenging and fun. Now to play the next Metro release :)

A great survival horror game that expands on the original, by updating graphics and creating a new more action packed game mode. I would recommend it for anyone, as it goes on sale often for up to 80% off, packaged with Metro: Last Light.

Aside from the very, VERY bad gun sound designs that take away from the "crunch" of combat, overall - a solid survival horror experience and a good entry point for the franchise. Hopping into Last Light next, see how things improve.

Sometimes you can find riches just outside of your comfort zone, a small leap of faith away. For me, that leap of faith was playing a game described as survival horror - Metro 2033. The 11 hours I spent playing this game is some of the most memorable time I have spent playing games in recent years.

The gameplay mechanics were simple yet nuanced - pumping your airguns, charging your nightvision, easy weapon upgrading.

The world was brilliant, teeming with details and polish, from citizens quarreling drunkenly as you pass a bar to enemies warming their hands by a barrel fire and sharing memories of their families.

The music and sound design was perfectly crafted to make your hair stand on end in the depths of a mushroom-clouded sewer, or inspire thoughts of heroism after your friends survive an onslaught of enemies at the door of a safe zone.

The combat was a little tough at times, considering how much movement the enemies do and how scarce ammo can be, but it really hit that sweet spot of every fight feeling like a struggle without becoming unwinnable.

I have a terrible time playing horror, so for me this game was about as suspenseful and terrifying as I can take. And thankfully I took the chance, because I think everyone should be able to experience Metro 2033 Redux.

I’ve been playing Metro 2033 Redux since it launched on PS4, and it still holds up as one of the best atmospheric shooters ever made. The post-apocalyptic Moscow setting is incredibly immersive — the dark tunnels, tense surface excursions, and constant sense of dread make every moment feel meaningful. The story is strong, the world-building is excellent, and the survival elements (gas mask filters, ammo scarcity, and careful movement) create a level of tension most games never achieve.

The Redux version cleans up the original nicely while keeping everything that made it special. The gunplay feels solid, the environments are packed with detail, and the overall mood is unmatched. It’s the kind of game that sticks with you long after you finish it.

If you care about atmospheric single-player experiences, Metro 2033 Redux is essential. It’s not just a good game — it’s one of those titles that belongs in any serious library.
